title: Cohomology above the number of projective coordinates
statement:
For any commutative ring $A$, any $n\ge0$, and any
quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ on
$\hyperref[def-pc-projective-space-twist]{\mathbf P^n_A}$,
one has $H^q(\mathbf P^n_A,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>n$.

proof.text: Let $P=\mathbf P^n_A$ and cover it by the $n+1$ standard opens $U_i=D_+(x_i)$ from [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Each $U_i$ is affine by [def-pc-proj]. Any finite intersection is $D_+(\prod_{i\in J}x_i)$ (a homogeneous prime avoids a product iff it avoids each factor), and $\prod_{i\in J}x_i$ is homogeneous of positive degree, hence the intersection is affine by the same standard-open description. Therefore [lem-pc-cech-computes] identifies $H^q(P,\mathcal F)$ with the Cech cohomology $\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ of this cover, and [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] (with the order $0<1<\dots<n$ on the indices) identifies $\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ with the cohomology of the alternating Cech complex. In degree $r$, that complex is the product over strictly increasing $(r+1)$-tuples, i.e. $(r+1)$-element subsets, of the $n+1$ indices. If $r>n$, there are no such subsets, so the degree-$r$ term is zero; all subsequent terms and differentials are zero, and the cohomology in degree $r$ is zero. Thus $H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>n$.
